narration: States are sitting on fifty-eight billion dollars of forgotten cash right now. You might be one of ten Americans who's owed an average of eight hundred and ninety-two dollars. Here's how to find out.
visual: Person silhouette with surprised expression; gold coins float upward away from them; '$58B' stat reveals at bottom. Dark background.

narration: It comes from things you've already forgotten — old bank accounts, uncashed paychecks, insurance refunds, security deposits. Your landlord moved on. Your old employer moved on. Your money just sat there.
visual: Four animated icon cards spring in one by one on light background: bank building, paycheck document, insurance shield, house deposit icon. Each labeled.

narration: There are forty million separate unclaimed accounts in the US right now. One in ten Americans is owed money, and the average amount is almost nine hundred dollars. And it never expires.
visual: Three dark stat cards animate in: counter counting up to '40M+ accounts waiting', '1 in 10 Americans', dollar counter animating to '$892 average'. Dark background.

narration: Claiming it costs nothing and takes under five minutes. Step one: search your full name. Step two: see what's listed. Step three: file a free claim. That's the entire process — completely legit.
visual: Three step rows spring in one by one on light background: magnifying glass 'Search your name', dollar circle 'See what you're owed', checkmark 'Claim it free'.

narration: Here's what most people miss — check every state you've ever lived in, not just where you are now. California holds twelve billion in unclaimed cash. New York holds nine billion. Most people find something in multiple states.
visual: Grid of colorful state cards animate in on dark background: CA $12B, NY $9B, TX $8B, FL $6B, IL $3B, OH $2.8B, PA $2.4B, WA $1.9B, GA $1.6B.

narration: Go to missingmoney.com — the official multi-state database — or search your state name plus 'unclaimed property.' Save this video right now. A thirty-second search might be worth almost a thousand dollars. Follow for more.
